The Section on Detailed Exposition (Paṭiniddesavāra) – Analysis 5
The Analysis of the Mode of Conveying Characteristics. Therein, what is the mode of conveying characteristics?
"When one single thing has been stated"—this is the mode of conveying characteristics.
What does it characterize?
When one phenomenon among those phenomena that share a single characteristic has been stated, the remaining phenomena have thereby been stated. How might this be?
As the Blessed One said:
“Bhikkhus, the eye is unstable, fleeting, limited, fragile, suffering for others, a calamity, wavering, a pit of embers, a conditioned formation, a murderer, and in the midst of enemies.
When this eye has been described, the remaining internal sense bases are thereby described as well.
For what reason?
Because all six internal sense bases have the single characteristic of being murderers.
And as the Blessed One said:

“Rādha, be indifferent toward past form; do not delight in future form; practice for the sake of disenchantment with, dispassion toward, the cessation of, the relinquishment of, and the letting go of present form.
When this aggregate of form has been stated, the remaining aggregates have also been stated.
For what reason?
For all five aggregates have been described in the Yamaka-vāda Sutta as having a single characteristic in the sense of being murderers.
And as the Blessed One said:
"Those for whom [the faculties] are well-undertaken..."
They constantly maintain mindfulness directed to the body;
they do not neglect what ought to be done,
but act with perseverance in what must be performed.
Thus, when mindfulness directed to the body is mentioned, mindfulness directed to feelings, to the mind, and to mental objects is also mentioned.
Likewise, when "whatever is seen, heard, sensed, or cognized" is mentioned, the "cognized" is included.
And as the Blessed One said:
“Therefore, bhikkhu, dwell contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world.
Herein, “ardent” refers to the faculty of energy; “clearly comprehending” refers to the faculty of wisdom; “mindful” refers to the faculty of mindfulness;
and “having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world” refers to the faculty of concentration. For one who dwells thus contemplating the body in the body, these four—
The foundations of mindfulness reach the fulfillment of their development.
For what reason? Because the four faculties have a single characteristic.
When the four foundations of mindfulness are being developed, the four right endeavors reach the fulfillment of their development.
When the four right efforts are being developed, the four bases of psychic power reach fulfillment through development;
when the four bases of psychic power are being developed, the five faculties reach fulfillment through development;
when the five faculties are being developed, the five powers reach fulfillment through development; when the five powers are being developed...
The seven factors of enlightenment reach fulfillment through development;

when the seven factors of enlightenment are being developed, the noble eightfold path reaches fulfillment through development; indeed, all the states conducive to enlightenment reach fulfillment through development.

For what reason? Because all factors conducive to enlightenment (*bodhipakkhiya*) have a single characteristic by virtue of the characteristic of leading to realization (*neyyānika*); because they possess this single characteristic, they reach the fulfillment of cultivation (*bhāvanā*).
Likewise, unwholesome states (*akusala-dhamma*), due to having a single characteristic, reach abandonment and disappearance.
When the four foundations of mindfulness (*satipaṭṭhāna*) are cultivated, the perversions (*vipallāsa*) are abandoned, and his nutriments (*āhāra*) come to full understanding (*pariññā*).
Through the clingings he becomes non-clinging; through the bonds he becomes detached; through the knots he becomes disjoined;
through the taints he becomes taintless; through the floods he has crossed over; through the arrows he is arrowless;
the stations of consciousness have been fully understood by him; and through the ways of going to ruin, he does not go to ruin.
In this way, unwholesome states also reach abandonment and disappearance because they share a single characteristic.
Furthermore, wherever the material faculty is taught, right there the material element, the aggregate of form, and the form base are also taught.
Or, wherever pleasant feeling is taught, right there the faculty of pleasure, the faculty of mental joy, and the noble truth of the origin of suffering are also taught.
Furthermore, wherever painful feeling is taught, there the faculty of pain, the faculty of mental grief, and the Noble Truth of suffering are taught.
Or, wherever neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is taught, there the faculty of equanimity and the entire dependent origination (paṭiccasamuppāda) are taught.
For what reason? Because ignorance underlies neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.

With ignorance as condition, volitional formations arise; with volitional formations as condition, consciousness arises; with consciousness as condition, name-and-form arises; with name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases arise;
with the six sense bases as condition, contact arises; with contact as condition, feeling arises; with feeling as condition, craving arises; with craving as condition, clinging arises;
with clinging as condition, existence arises; with existence as condition, birth arises; with birth as condition, aging and death arise.
Sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise; such is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.

And that [suffering] is to be abandoned by means of the side of defilement characterized by lust, hatred, and delusion, and it is to be abandoned by means of the noble qualities characterized by the absence of lust, the absence of hatred, and the absence of delusion.

Thus, when one phenomenon among those phenomena—which possess the same characteristic in terms of function, essential mark, generality, and passing away and rebirth—is stated, the remaining phenomena are thereby stated as well.
Therefore the Venerable Mahākaccāyana said: "When a single dhamma has been stated.
The Mode of Conveying Characteristics (lakkhaṇa-hāra) is concluded.
